tasks.short: Run the session on the floor as practice, role-play or a short talk.

today.trigger: A session is on the calendar, or a team lead asks for a toolbox talk on one task.
steps: Check who is rostered and which site rules apply in AFAS and Studytube.
Pick a format from the last PowerPoint: talk, role-play, video or practice.
Rewrite the exercise so it fits this crew, this site and this shift length.
Run the session in the room, on Teams or at the start of the shift.
Write down attendance and what the crew could not do.
drudgery: Rewriting the same exercise for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Searching SharePoint for the last deck that matched the live dock rule.
today.time_sinks: The evening of preparation, then the session itself, then chasing who was actually on the shift.

lenses.faster: Rewriting the exercise per site and hunting for the last good deck disappear, about a third of the hours. The session stays, plus a short check of the draft, so about a quarter of the task time goes.
lenses.autonomous: A booked session or a team-lead request starts it. A draft exercise is prepared from the approved procedure before the specialist opens it. The specialist approves the exercise and runs the session.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift crews get a 20-minute practice on one real task at the start of the shift, which daytime classrooms now take. If that practice is cheap to prepare, team leads on nights will ask for more, until the roster cannot spare the people.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the same role-play three times. The specialist wants the debrief on the floor, watching whether the person can do the step.
lenses.options: A role-play, a supervised practice on a real pallet, or a short video changes what a tired crew will finish in 20 minutes. That choice changes the session, not only the prep time.
lenses.altitude: The week has fewer nights of slide edits and more short debriefs on the shift. The specialist decides which technique a crew will finish, and the job becomes more expert about learning on a shift and less about producing formats.
reach: The HR business partner's practice talk with a new team lead on how to give one piece of feedback. The specialist would need to learn where a skills practice ends and the performance cycle begins.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist sees whether this crew understood, stops an exercise that would shame someone in front of colleagues, and judges fatigue and language on a night shift. A qualified instructor still runs any practical safety test.
tasks.pattern_why: The specialist stays in front of the crew because the next step depends on their questions and on what they can safely practise. A model can draft the exercise inside a known session plan. It should not lead the session.

in_practice.trigger: A session is booked, or a team lead asks for a practice on one named task.
steps: A draft exercise is written from the approved procedure and the site card, in plain Dutch.
The specialist edits it and picks the one format that fits the shift length.
The specialist runs the session with the crew.
The crew does the step and explains it back.
The exercise version and the attendance are filed.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves the exercise before it is used and stops the session if the crew cannot practise safely. A qualified instructor runs any forklift, VCA or food-safety practical.
data_needed: Approved procedure and site card
Shift length and site
Language already used on that site's safety card
People rostered for the session
Certificate the task supports
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint session record with exercise version, approver and attendance. No camera recording and no attention or emotion score.

evidence.claim: Across 531 self-selected L&D practitioners, faster content was still the top expected benefit of AI, while privacy was the top barrier at 52%.
Workday's check-in agent drafted manager feedback against a Situation-Behavior-Impact rubric. From a 36% Good baseline on 12,200 write-ups, users gained 16 points and non-users 7.
In a randomised trial with 52 junior developers, people who used AI scored 17% lower on a mastery quiz, while those who asked for explanations kept more.
An AI tutor must be identified as AI, and inferring learners' emotions, including from a webcam, is prohibited.
evidence.source: EU AI Act Art. 50 and Art. 5(1)(f), https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/50/

risks: A fluent role-play can still teach a dock step that is wrong for that site.
Learners who watch a generated answer instead of explaining the step are likely to keep less, as in the developer trial.
Recording a session or scoring attention would need works-council consent under WOR 27(1)(l) and can cross the emotion-inference ban.
A generated clip that looks like a real colleague must be disclosed and is a poor fit for a safety briefing.
research_questions: Will team leads release 20 minutes at the start of a night shift when volume is high?
Which format, role-play, supervised practice or video, is finished more often on nights, and does a later instructor check show fewer errors?
Does asking the worker to explain the step beat a video they only watch, on a check one week later?
Will the works council treat an AI-drafted exercise used with crews as a training-policy change that needs consent?

tasks.short: Write and update the manuals, cards and course packs.

today.trigger: A procedure changes, a course is out of date, or a new-hire pack is missing a site card.
steps: Find the current PDF, PowerPoint or Word file on SharePoint.
Copy the old manual or sit with a team lead for the changed step.
Draft the handout, the slides and the questions as separate files.
Mail the draft around and wait for comments.
Load the finished file into Studytube.
drudgery: Hunting version 7 of the same procedure on SharePoint.
Reformatting one text into a handout, a slide and a Studytube page.
today.time_sinks: Waiting for comments, then rewriting after someone finds an old dock rule in the text.

lenses.faster: Writing the first full draft from a blank page disappears. A check of the steps, a floor walk when the dock rule changed, and the safety lead's sign-off stay, a bit under half of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A changed procedure, a changed certificate name, or a missing site card starts it. One draft step returns a card, a handout and questions. The specialist edits, and the safety lead signs safety content before anyone is enrolled.
lenses.ambitious: The three staffing agencies get a new service: a one-page site card in the flex order pack, before the first shift. If that card is cheap, agencies will ask for it on short peak-season assignments they now send out with a thick PDF.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss searching SharePoint for the latest file. The specialist wants an hour with a reach-truck driver to see which sentence the manual got wrong.
lenses.options: A full manual, a one-page card, or the same card in the second language already used on that site's safety signs changes whether a flex worker can use it on night one. The format changes what is safe to approve.
lenses.altitude: The week becomes review and floor checks rather than drafting. The specialist can block a text that is not safe to put in a new hire's hand, and the job becomes more expert on the live warehouse and less on layout.
reach: The HR administrator's assembly of the new-hire document pack from SharePoint templates. The specialist would need to learn which pages are learning material and which are part of the AFAS contract or the CAO.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist can tell a dangerous sentence from a clumsy one, because they have walked the dock, the lockout and the trailer stand. An external body still certifies VCA and forklift skill. The safety lead signs those texts.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call can turn an approved PDF or a title into a draft card, script and questions inside Studytube. The steps are known in advance. A person still checks the warehouse facts, and the safety lead signs safety content.

in_practice.trigger: A procedure, certificate name or site rule changes, or a flex order needs a site card that is not on file.
steps: The current PDF or SharePoint page is passed to Studytube AI Authoring.
The draft comes back as a short card, a handout and questions.
The specialist checks every operational step against the live process.
The safety lead signs any pack that teaches forklift, dock, VCA or food-safety steps.
The approved file is versioned on SharePoint and loaded into Studytube.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist releases ordinary process material after the edit. The safety lead signs safety content before enrolment opens.
data_needed: Current approved procedure
Certificate name and site
Reading level the floor already uses
The second language already printed on that site's safety card
The CAO or arbo point the text must keep intact
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history with the editor and, where required, the safety-lead signature, plus the Studytube course id.

evidence.claim: Studytube AI Authoring drafts outlines, scripts and questions from a title or an uploaded PDF, PowerPoint or SCORM, and authors edit. The vendor claims a course within minutes.
MHR's learning team has an agent draft content and check reading level, with a person reviewing. The published account gives no outcome measure.
US desk workers in a BambooHR study spent 42% of their AI time troubleshooting and 35% on the work itself.
Outside bodies certify VCA and forklift skills. AI can prepare learners and cannot issue those certificates.

risks: A fluent Dutch draft can contain a wrong dock or lockout step that a reading-level check will pass.
Fixing weak drafts can eat the time the draft was meant to save.
Pasting internal procedures and any personal data into a tool outside the Studytube tenant conflicts with AVG and with the privacy barrier L&D staff already report.
A new authoring tool that can also track learners needs works-council consent under WOR 27 before it is switched on.
research_questions: What share of current packs is safety-critical (forklift, dock, VCA, food) versus office procedure, and how many days does the safety lead need to sign one?
Does Studytube AI Authoring keep the meaning of Noordhaven's Dutch arbo and CAO terms from the source PDF?
On a sample of 10 changed procedures, how many draft steps are wrong against the live site, and is the fix faster than writing the one-page card?
Can the flex site card go out in the agency order without placing employee personal data in the agency portal?

tasks.short: Get each worker onto the course they need and onto the roster.

today.trigger: A certificate is near its end date, a new hire has a start date, or a manager asks for a skill.
steps: Pull completions from Studytube and the role from AFAS, often via Excel.
Choose the programme that fits the role and the site.
Mail the employee and the team lead with possible dates.
Book a room or a Teams link around the published roster.
Chase no-shows and people whose card then lapses anyway.
drudgery: Copying names between Studytube, Excel and mail.
The chase mail to three sites and to agencies for flex workers.
today.time_sinks: Finding a training seat that does not break the shift, then discovering the certificate date was empty or old.

lenses.faster: Building the list and sending chase mail disappear for people who match the matrix and have a training seat. Exceptions, flex workers and talks with team leads stay, a little over half of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A certificate entering its renewal window, or a start date in AFAS, starts the job. It enrols people who match the written matrix and have a free training seat. The specialist decides every exception, and a team lead can reverse a standard booking within two working days.
lenses.ambitious: Each time the night roster for Tilburg or Venlo is published, the planner gets a decision they now make only after a lapse or a quarterly chase: whether this crew still holds the cards for that work. If the check is cheap, the three agencies will ask for the same answer on a flex order.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the expiry chase. The specialist wants the talk with a team lead about what productive looks like at day 30.
lenses.options: A classroom day, a 20-minute drill at shift start, or an e-learning module changes whether a driver is taken off a truck. That choice changes the roster and the pay hours, not only the specialist's effort.
lenses.altitude: The week is exceptions and conversations, after a one-time agreement on the matrix with the works council. The specialist decides the cases the matrix must not touch, including flex, empty dates and reintegration, and becomes more expert in those judgments and less occupied by the chase.
reach: The recruiter's check, before an offer is sent in Recruitee, that a required VCA or forklift card will be valid on day one. The specialist would need to learn the offer stage and which conditions the recruiter may put in the offer.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides the cases a matrix must not enrol: a flex worker whose record is incomplete, someone on adjusted duties under Wet verbetering poortwachter, and a request to train a skill the role does not need. The model and the job must not declare a person skilled.
tasks.pattern_why: The programme required to keep a role legal on the shift can be written as role, site, certificate and expiry. A scheduled job can read Studytube and AFAS. A model is not needed for that match. Developmental requests stay with the specialist.

in_practice.trigger: A certificate date enters the renewal window, AFAS receives a start date, or a manager asks for a skill that is not in the matrix.
steps: The job reads role, site, certificate dates and the published roster.
An empty expiry date, a flex worker, adjusted duties, or no free training seat goes to the specialist.
Where the matrix matches and a training seat is free, the job enrols the person in Studytube and tells the team lead.
The specialist agrees each exception with the team lead or the HR business partner and enrols by hand.
The team lead may reverse a matrix booking within two working days.
in_practice.human_gate: The works council agrees the matrix as training policy before any automatic enrolment starts. After that, the specialist decides every exception, and a team lead can reverse a standard booking within two working days.
data_needed: Role, site and shift
Certificate name and expiry, with empty dates treated as exceptions
A free training seat on the roster
Contract type and agency assignment end date
A reintegration or adjusted-duties flag from AFAS
The paid-hours code Payroll uses for a training day
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube enrolment log and the AFAS certificate field. Exception reasons go on the SharePoint training log. The job does not write to the appraisal.

evidence.claim: A written role-to-certificate matrix plus Studytube expiry dates and AFAS roster seats can drive enrolment without a model. No opened case in this digest shows a logistics firm running that job.
Microsoft's Learning agent shows skill gaps, pathways and mentors. HR still guides role moves and leadership development, and no outcome figures are published.
From 2 December 2027, AI that uses learning data to evaluate workers is high-risk, with a trained overseer, six-month logs, and workers' representatives informed.
evidence.source: EU AI Act Annex III 4(b) and Art. 26, https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/annex/3/

evidence.claim: Works-council consent is required for training policy and for rules on personal data, and a missing consent can be nullified within one month.

risks: An empty or stale date, treated as valid, would put an uncertified person on the roster.
Adding absence, manager notes or a performance score to the rule would turn it into worker evaluation and, from 2 December 2027, into high-risk AI.
Flex-worker training records shared with an agency can breach AVG if the basis and the fields are not agreed.
Automatic booking of paid training hours can conflict with the warehouse CAO or the transport CAO if the pay code is wrong.
research_questions: Is the role-to-certificate matrix written in AFAS or Studytube today, and what share of employee rows have an empty expiry?
Which CAO article pays training hours for warehouse staff and for drivers, and can AFAS receive that code from the enrolment?
Where does a flex worker's training record live when the assignment ends, and what is the AVG basis for keeping it?
If the roster check had existed last quarter, how many published shifts would have included a lapsed or empty card?

tasks.short: See if a course worked, and record what we measured.

today.trigger: Month end, a business partner asks whether a course was worth the shift time, or the training plan is reviewed.
steps: Export completions from Studytube.
Paste them into Excel and try to match people and sites from AFAS.
Read the few evaluation forms that came back.
Build a PowerPoint or hand-edit a page because the nightly Power BI extract does not yet show courses well.
Talk through the numbers with the HR business partner.
drudgery: Cleaning exports so site and shift match the HR dashboard.
Chasing evaluation forms that never come back.
today.time_sinks: Making the numbers agree before anyone will discuss whether the course should continue.

lenses.faster: Exporting Studytube, cleaning Excel and rebuilding slides disappear. Reading the page, checking small groups and the meeting with the HR business partner stay, about 60% of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: Six weeks after an intake group, or the monthly training review, starts it. Power BI refreshes the counts and one pass clusters anonymous comments. The specialist writes the conclusion with the HR business partner.
lenses.ambitious: The HR business partner and the site manager get a decision they now make yearly, if at all: six weeks after each intake group, whether that group is on track for day 90. If the page is cheap to refresh, they will ask for it for small groups they now skip.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss pasting exports into Excel. The specialist wants the conversation about why one site's week-one completion is low.
lenses.options: Judging a course on completions, or on week-one onboarding done and still employed at day 90, changes whether the course is kept. The two frames change the decision. The figures stay at site and shift, never on a named person.
lenses.altitude: The week has a short review with each HR business partner instead of a report build. The specialist can recommend that a programme stop when it does not move week-one completion or 90-day retention, and the job becomes more expert in those measures and less in assembling files.
reach: The People Analytics analyst's monthly training page on the HR Power BI dashboard. The specialist would need to learn the nightly AFAS extract, how a Studytube file joins it, and how to keep every visual at site and shift level.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist can say when a movement is too thin to act on, and can keep a comment from a small night crew out of the page so it cannot become a judgment on a named worker. The conclusion stays with the specialist and the HR business partner.
tasks.pattern_why: The counts belong in Power BI. One model call can cluster comment text that has already had names removed. The workflow is fixed, and the specialist writes the conclusion. An agent is not needed.

in_practice.trigger: Six weeks after an intake group starts, and again at the monthly training review.
steps: Power BI refreshes completions, the week-one flag and leavers by site and shift.
One pass clusters comment text after names and personnel numbers are removed.
The specialist reads the page and drops any theme that could identify a person.
The specialist and the HR business partner compare the result with the measure they agreed at the start.
They record keep, change or stop for the programme.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist writes the conclusion. The review is not written to an individual appraisal in AFAS. A theme that could identify someone on a small crew is removed before the meeting.
data_needed: Programme id, site, shift and group size
Completion and the week-one onboarding flag
Employment status at day 90
Comment text with names and personnel numbers removed
The measure the manager agreed before the programme started
in_practice.logs_to: The existing HR Power BI dataset at group level, and a short conclusion on SharePoint. Comment text is not stored with a personnel number.

evidence.claim: MHR agrees measures with the manager first, collects them at six weeks and six months, and uses AI to cluster comments as a support for the reviewer. The account is unmeasured and says the tool is not for decision-making.
No opened page in the Workday account shows a course cutting time-to-skill. Workday advises setting baselines before launch.
Using learning data in AI that evaluates workers becomes high-risk from 2 December 2027. Monitoring-capable tools need works-council consent.
evidence.source: EU AI Act Annex III 4(b), https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/annex/3/ ; WOR art. 27, https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0002747

risks: A dashboard of named people would become a second appraisal and would need works-council consent, with nullity risk within one month.
On a small night crew, a comment cluster can identify the person even after the name is removed.
Completions can rise while week-one readiness and 90-day retention do not.
The nightly Power BI extract is AFAS-based today, so a Studytube join can be wrong on site, shift or flex workers.
research_questions: Can Studytube completions join the nightly AFAS extract at site and shift, with names kept off the dashboard?
Do six-week measures, agreed before the course, move week-one completion or 90-day retention, or only completions?
Will the works council consent to comment clustering if the same tool could also be used to monitor individuals?
How many evaluation comments arrive in a normal month, and is that enough to cluster?

tasks.short: Plan induction and the training calendar for the three sites.

today.trigger: A group of new hires has start dates in AFAS, or a site asks to rerun induction.
steps: Get start dates, roles and sites from AFAS and the recruiter.
Build a day-by-day plan: safety, buddy, systems and site tour.
Book instructors, rooms and Teams links.
Send the plan to the manager.
Rebuild it when the shift, the buddy or the start date changes.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same timetable after one roster change.
Holding a Rotterdam classroom that the Venlo night starter cannot attend.
today.time_sinks: The mail between recruiter, site manager and instructor before the plan is stable.

lenses.faster: Rebuilding the timetable and rebooking rooms when one date moves get much shorter. The talks with the site manager, the recruiter and the buddy stay, about 70% of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A start date in AFAS, or a site request for an induction date, starts it. A draft schedule proposes rooms and instructors around the roster. The specialist and the site manager agree the plan before it is sent.
lenses.ambitious: Flex workers and night-shift starters get a first-week plan built around their first three shifts, a service they are not designed for today. If that plan is cheap, agencies will push more short peak-season assignments through it.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss redrawing the calendar each time a buddy is absent. The specialist wants to set the week-one buddy standard with the three site managers.
lenses.options: One shared Thursday in Rotterdam, or a plan fitted to the first three shifts at the home site, changes who is cleared to work the dock in week one. The two plans are different decisions.
lenses.altitude: The week is design with site managers, with the calendar draft already in hand. The specialist sets the week-one standard for each site and shift, and the job becomes more expert in that standard and less in room booking.
reach: The recruiter's handover of what was promised in the Recruitee offer about the first week. The specialist would need to learn the offer stage and which first-week promises are already written to the candidate.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist knows which buddy will actually teach, and whether a plan is fair across sites and shifts enough to take to the works council. They also see when adjusted duties under Wet verbetering poortwachter make the standard week unsafe.
tasks.pattern_why: The specialist remains the lead because the plan depends on the site, the buddy and what the recruiter already promised. Software can propose dates from the roster. The design itself is not a rule that should run alone.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS receives a start date, or a site manager asks for an induction date.
steps: The specialist checks role, site, shift and which certificate must be valid before the first productive shift.
A schedule draft proposes rooms and instructors around the published roster.
The specialist agrees the week-one plan with the site manager and names a buddy who is on that shift.
The plan is checked against what the recruiter promised in the offer.
The plan goes to the new hire and the manager, and into Studytube.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist and the site manager agree the plan before it is sent. The specialist decides when the standard does not fit a night start, a flex assignment or adjusted duties.
data_needed: Start date, role, site and shift pattern
Certificates still open
Buddy's roster and absence
Offer notes from Recruitee
The week-one standard the works council has already seen
in_practice.logs_to: The orientation standard on SharePoint, and the person's own plan on the AFAS or Studytube record.

evidence.claim: MHR agrees the measures with the manager before collecting them at six weeks and six months. Design of the programme stays with the learning team.
Training policy needs works-council consent under WOR 27(1)(f). A change to the induction standard can fall under that consent.
No opened source shows a course design cutting time-to-skill. Week-one completion and 90-day retention are the measures Noordhaven can check.

risks: A clean timetable can still name a buddy who is absent or on another shift.
One company-wide Thursday favours Rotterdam day staff and fails a Venlo night start.
A reintegration plan can conflict with a standard induction that puts someone on the dock.
Changing the week-one standard without the works council can be nullified.
research_questions: What is written down today as onboarding completed in week one, and is it stored in AFAS or Studytube?
Can a night-shift starter and a flex worker finish that standard without the Rotterdam daytime session?
Which induction items are a legal or CAO must before the work starts, and which are local habit?
Does the works council expect to consent before a site changes its week-one plan?

tasks.short: Choose classroom, Teams or on the site, using cost and results.

today.trigger: A course is coming up and someone asks whether it can run on Teams, or a travel bill arrives.
steps: List who must attend and from which site.
Estimate room, travel and hours off the shift in Excel.
Look up how the last run went in person or online.
Write a short note and discuss it with the site manager.
Book the mode that the loudest constraint forces, often habit.
drudgery: Rebuilding the travel sheet for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Guessing the cost of a lost shift because the rate sits with Finance.
today.time_sinks: The same argument is repeated for every run because the last choice and its result are not stored.

lenses.faster: Building the travel and hours spreadsheet by hand disappears. Checking the three figures and agreeing the mode with the site manager stay, about two thirds of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A proposed course date and headcount start the comparison. The job prepares three modes with hours, travel, room cost and last completion. The specialist approves the mode before anyone is booked.
lenses.ambitious: The controller gets a decision far more often than the yearly training budget talk: before each large run, which of three modes to buy, with backfill euros written down. If the sheet is cheap, FP&A will ask for it on smaller runs too.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the spreadsheet. The specialist wants a serious choice with the controller about backfill versus a day in the classroom.
lenses.options: Classroom, Teams, or a short session at shift start changes the hours off the truck, the travel and whether a practical skill is practised at all. The three scenarios are the decision.
lenses.altitude: Once a month the specialist sits with the controller and the site manager on the large runs, with the sheet already filled. They gain the right to recommend the mode on cost and last result, the site manager still releases people, and the job becomes more expert in that tradeoff.
reach: The controller's note that explains training spend and backfill for a large course run. The specialist would need to learn the backfill rate Finance uses and how a training day is posted in AFAS.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist holds the line when the cheaper mode cannot teach the skill. Forklift, VCA practice and food-safety practice stay in person with a qualified instructor. The controller can see the euros. The specialist can see whether the person will be safe on the first shift.
tasks.pattern_why: Travel, hours off shift, room cost and past completion by mode can be calculated from AFAS, Studytube and a Finance rate. Those rules fit in software. A model does not make the choice safer. The specialist approves each mode.

in_practice.trigger: A programme is proposed with a date and a headcount.
steps: The job builds three options: a classroom day, a Teams session, and a short session at shift start.
Each option shows hours off shift, travel between the three sites, room cost and the last completion for that mode.
Any practical certificate is marked in-person with a qualified instructor.
The specialist and the site manager choose the mode. The controller sees the line when the amount is material.
The booking is made in Outlook and Studytube, and the choice is stored.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves the mode before anyone is booked. Forklift, VCA practice and food-safety practice are in person with a qualified instructor.
data_needed: Headcount by site and shift
Travel time between Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo
Backfill rate and room cost from Finance
Past completion by mode and programme
Whether the skill is a practical certificate
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint decision note with the three figures, the mode chosen, the approver and the date to look again.

evidence.claim: No source in the digest measures in-person against virtual delivery on cost and skill for warehouse work. A comparison sheet can still be built from roster hours and a Finance rate.
Workday advises baselines before launch, and no opened page shows a course cutting time-to-skill.
Outside bodies certify VCA and forklift skills, so those practicals cannot be replaced by a virtual session.

risks: A virtual booking can be chosen to save backfill on a skill that has to be practised on the equipment.
Without a real backfill rate the sheet looks exact and is only a guess.
An environmental line with no agreed factor would decorate the decision. Completion differences by mode may be site and role mix, not the mode.
The site manager can be talked over by a spreadsheet if the approval is treated as a formality.
research_questions: Does Finance already have an hourly backfill rate per site that L&D may use?
For which courses did a Teams run fail a later practical or an external VCA or forklift exam?
After holding role and site constant, do completion and 90-day retention differ by mode?
Is travel between the three sites large enough, against backfill, to change the mode on a typical run?

tasks.short: Keep up with learning practice, the CAO and the AI rules.

today.trigger: A weekly reading habit, a CAO or VCA update, or a vendor mail about AI in Studytube or Microsoft 365.
steps: Scan journals, newsletters and the inbox.
Save items about the CAO, arbo, VCA, forklift and the AI Act.
Read the few that look as if they change a course or a duty.
Tell a colleague when a course or the works-council file should change.
drudgery: Vendor newsletters and the same item forwarded twice.
Summaries that never say what Noordhaven should do on Monday.
today.time_sinks: Reading time that does not land in a course change or in the file for the works council.

lenses.faster: Skimming newsletters and duplicate mail disappears. Reading the primary text that might change a course or the measures file stays, about two thirds of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A weekly slot, or a announced change in the CAO, the VCA scheme or AI Act guidance, starts a one-page brief with source links. The specialist reads the items that touch Noordhaven and decides what is updated.
lenses.ambitious: The HR Director and the works council get a new service: an Article 4 measures file for staff who use AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and Microsoft 365, updated when a tool or the official guidance changes. If the brief is cheap, every new AI add-on will need a line, so demand grows with the tool count.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss skimming vendor mail. The specialist wants to read the AI Act article and the CAO training clause properly, then write one clear note.
lenses.options: Three sources in one week, an EU guidance page, a CAO clause and a VCA scheme note, can point to different actions. Which one the specialist opens changes what goes on the works-council agenda.
lenses.altitude: Reading time moves to the few primary texts that can change a course or the measures file. The specialist can tell the HR Director that a proposed learning tool is not yet fit to take to the works council, and the job becomes more expert in that judgment if the source is still read.
reach: The HR Director's written note to the works council when training policy or a learning tool changes. The specialist would need to learn which WOR 27 items need consent, and which sentences the director still has to say in the meeting.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist can tell a relevant change from a vendor slogan, including a paid AI-literacy certificate that is only an attendance record. They judge what the CAO, these three sites and this works council need. That judgment depends on reading the source.
tasks.pattern_why: One call can turn a saved set of public items into a one-page brief that keeps the source links. The specialist still reads anything that might change a course, the CAO practice or the Article 4 file. The steps do not vary enough to need an agent.

in_practice.trigger: Once a week, and whenever a CAO, VCA scheme or official AI Act update is announced.
steps: One pass summarises the new public items and vendor notes the specialist has already saved, each with its link.
Employee records and internal cases stay out of the prompt.
The specialist reads every item that touches a course, the CAO, the works council or Article 4.
They update the measures file when a tool or a duty has changed.
They send the HR Director a note only when the works-council agenda or a course should change.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist decides what is relevant and what Noordhaven will change. A summary, or a vendor certificate, is never the measure taken under Article 4.
data_needed: The source list: official EU and Dutch texts, CAO updates, VCA and forklift scheme notes
The current Article 4 measures file
The list of AI tools employees already use
No employee records and no absence or appraisal text
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint Article 4 measures file: date, source link, what was read, and what Noordhaven changed.

evidence.claim: Since 27 July 2026, Article 4 requires measures so staff have sufficient AI literacy. It sets no level, hours, test or certificate. Supervision applies from 2 August 2026.
A Dutch EUR 295 course still claims a voldoende level and sells a certificate. That certificate is a record of attendance, not proof the Article 4 duty is met.
Developers who used AI scored 17% lower on a later mastery quiz. Reading only summaries would thin the specialist's own judgment the same way.
Privacy is the top reported barrier to AI in L&D, cited by 52% of practitioners in the Learning News survey.

risks: A weekly brief that is skimmed and never opened would replace reading and weaken the specialist's judgment.
A bought certificate can be mistaken for compliance with Article 4.
Sending internal cases or employee text to a public model conflicts with AVG. Vendor newsletters can crowd out the official text.
The brief can look like a decision. The duty is the measures Noordhaven actually takes.
research_questions: Which tools in daily use, Studytube AI, Microsoft 365 Copilot, AFAS, scanners, fall under the Article 4 duty today, and who is the named overseer?
Does a weekly brief change what is put on the works-council agenda over two months, or does it go unread?
Which Dutch sources announce VCA and forklift scheme changes, and can the brief read them without an employee sending internal files?
How many minutes a week are now spent fixing a bad summary versus reading the source?

tasks.short: Check an instructor's outline and handouts before we use them.

today.trigger: An internal instructor or an external trainer sends an outline, a text or a handout.
steps: Read the pack against the current procedure and the certificate name.
Mark reading level, old steps and missing practice.
Mail the comments back to the instructor.
Check the next version, often the day before the session.
File the approved pack on SharePoint.
drudgery: Chasing the next version by mail.
today.time_sinks: Packs that arrive the day before the session, so the check is a glance.

lenses.faster: The first markup for reading level, old dates and missing practice disappears. Judging the flagged lines and the safety-lead sign-off stay, about half of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: An uploaded outline or handout starts one check against the current procedure, the certificate name and a reading-level rule. The specialist decides accept or return. The safety lead signs safety content.
lenses.ambitious: The safety lead gets a new service: a checked pack for every external forklift, VCA or food-safety instructor before they teach, not only for the internal courses. If the first pass is cheap, agency trainers in peak season will be put through the same check.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss marking up fonts. The specialist wants the argument with an instructor about a warehouse step that is wrong.
lenses.options: Accept, return with marked lines, or send to the safety lead are three different outcomes for the same pack. A plain-language rewrite versus a procedure-exact rewrite changes what the instructor is told to fix, and can change whether the pack is used.
lenses.altitude: The week is time on the flagged lines and with the safety lead, not a full reread of every slide. The specialist can stop an external trainer's pack before it reaches a crew, and becomes more expert on the procedure and less of a proofreader.
reach: The HR business partner's check that a site's local instruction sheet still matches the company procedure. The specialist would need to learn how a site complaint reaches the business partner, and which document wins when the local sheet and the company procedure differ.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist catches a plausible step that is wrong for the current Tilburg or Venlo layout, which a reading-level score will pass. They send safety content to the safety lead. They do not become the body that certifies the skill.
tasks.pattern_why: One call can compare a pack with the current procedure and a fixed checklist: reading level, certificate name, old steps, missing practice, and a label where text was generated. The specialist still judges the flags. The check is the same each time, so an agent is unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: An instructor uploads an outline, a text or a handout for a named course.
steps: One pass compares the pack with the current procedure, the certificate name and the reading-level rule.
It marks old steps, missing practice and any generated section that is not labelled.
The specialist reviews every flagged line and every safety step.
The safety lead signs forklift, dock, VCA and food-safety content.
The pack is approved or returned, and the version is stored before Studytube enrolment opens.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist decides accept or return. The safety lead signs safety content before the pack can be used with a crew.
data_needed: Current approved procedure for that site
Certificate name and whether an external body owns the exam
The reading level already used on site cards
A label when a section was generated by a model
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint pack record with version, checklist result, specialist decision and the safety-lead signature where the content is safety.

evidence.claim: MHR's agent drafts content and checks reading level, and a person reviews before the material is used. No result is published.
Studytube AI Authoring produces drafts an author then edits. The same review standard can be applied to an instructor's upload.
Desk workers spent 42% of AI time troubleshooting output. A checklist that only finds style will miss a wrong operational step.
Scoring the instructor as a worker with an AI tool would move toward high-risk worker evaluation from 2 December 2027.

risks: A reading-level pass on a dangerous step would give false confidence.
If the specialist signs safety content alone, Noordhaven treats L&D as the certifying body.
Using the checklist to score the instructor, rather than the pack, would need works-council consent and could become high-risk AI.
External trainers and agencies may send packs too late in peak season for the safety lead to sign them.
research_questions: On the last 20 instructor packs, were the real defects wrong steps, or mostly reading level and format?
How often would the checklist accept a sentence the safety lead then rejects?
Is there a written standard, reading level, source procedure, certificate name and a label for generated text, that the check can run against?
Will agencies accept a returned pack in peak season, or will sessions go ahead without it?

role.altitude: The two specialists move from a week of producing courses and chasing certificates to keeping two things true for about 1,200 people: the competence record that says who may work which shift, and the Article 4 measures file the works council can read. They can hold a booking when a card is missing, stop an unsafe pack, and set the week-one standard with the site managers. The HR Director still decides leadership development and speaks in the works council. The job becomes more expert in warehouse competence and the legal file, and less of a slide studio.
reach: The HR administrator's update of certificate dates on the AFAS record, after the specialist learns which field Payroll and an auditor read.
The recruiter's certificate condition on the Recruitee offer, after the specialist learns the offer stage.
The People Analytics analyst's training page on the HR Power BI dashboard, kept at site and shift.
The controller's backfill note for a large course run, after the specialist learns Finance's rate.
The drafting of the HR Director's works-council note when training policy or a learning tool changes. The director keeps the seat in the meeting.
role.ceiling_note: Two people at a loaded cost of EUR 68 an hour cannot be on every shift at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Practical tests, safety-lead signatures and external VCA and forklift exams stay outside the role. Works-council consent sets the pace for any new tool. Evaluation stays at group level, so this role does not take individual appraisal, the payroll close or the performance cycle.
skills_to_grow: AFAS certificate fields, the paid-hours code for a training day, and the adjusted-duties flag used in Wet verbetering poortwachter.
Studytube administration: expiries, enrolments and review of AI-authored drafts.
The Article 4 measures file, and which WOR 27 items need works-council consent.
Reading the HR Power BI page and Finance's backfill rate without building a second dashboard.
Plain Dutch at the reading level of the floor, and a clear handoff to the safety lead.
role.ambitious_version: L&D keeps mandatory competence valid before the roster is published, for permanent staff and for flex workers, and runs a week-one path that fits the site and the shift. Office staff can receive a pathway the specialist approves. Practical safety stays with a qualified instructor and the external examiner. The file for Article 4 is current for the tools people actually use. The measures that matter are week-one onboarding done, a valid certificate on the first shift, and still employed at day 90.
